messages:
elena: :rotating_light: Alert - unusual 5xx surge in eu1 (eu1-az-b) for hosted inference. Metrics show 502/504 spike starting ~09:02 UTC. Support already has an open escalation from Fugu Inc reporting timeouts and failed auth attempts.

maria: Customer says requests time out then sometimes return 502. They see auth failures intermittently too. Pasted their sample curl: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> sometimes 200, sometimes 502.

jamal: I'm on it. Can someone grab a quick region-level pcap or netstat from the gateway hosts? I'll correlate with edge metrics.

kai: Starting packet capture on eu1-az-b gateway nodes (gw-azb-1 / gw-azb-2). Running `tcpdump -n -s 96 -c 10000 port 443` - will upload to /tmp and paste gist.

sre-bot: Monitoring note: gateway 5xx rate by az: eu1-az-a 1.2% -> 1.5%, eu1-az-b 6.3% -> 19.7%, eu1-az-c 1.0% -> 1.1%. Request latency P50/P90 increased in az-b.

maria: Escalation from Fugu: "requests for our EU users are failing consistently between 09:00-09:12 UTC, page shows 502s and auth token errors." They gave a test trace showing routing hops flapping.

jamal: I pulled a short tcpdump, seeing lots of retransmits and occasional out-of-order. Suspect packet loss between our edge and provider transit. Snippet:

```
09:06:14.123456 IP 10.0.12.34.443 > 10.100.5.8.52000: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12412, ack 54321, win 64240, length 67
09:06:14.223789 IP 10.0.12.34.443 > 10.100.5.8.52000: Flags [F.], seq 12412, ack 54321, win 64240, length 0
09:06:14.324012 IP 10.100.5.8.52000 > 10.0.12.34.443: Flags [R], seq 54321, ack 12412, win 0
--- retransmit count high, tcp retransmit and dup-ack patterns ---
```

kai: I also ran traceroute from gw-azb-1 to a sample client IP (provided by Fugu). See hop 6/7 timing spikes and *some* packet loss:

```
traceroute to 203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  gw-azb-1 (10.0.12.1)  0.453 ms  0.411 ms  0.398 ms
 2  provider-peering-1 (198.51.100.2)  2.34 ms  2.28 ms  2.31 ms
 3  provider-core-3 (198.51.100.10)  20.1 ms  120.4 ms  20.2 ms
 4  provider-agg-2 (198.51.100.14)  21.0 ms  21.1 ms  200.3 ms
 5  203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45)  22.0 ms  22.5 ms  22.3 ms
```

jamal: The 120ms/200ms spikes at hops 3/4 indicate intermittent microbursts or buffering at provider side. I'm opening a ticket with the transit provider and attaching pcap + traceroute.

maria: Is there a fast mitigation we can do for Fugu while provider investigates? They need <200ms p95 and <1% 5xx.

kai: Short-term: routing failover to eu2 could help if customer is tolerant of cross-region (Fugu said EU users must stay EU, but eu2 is in EU region; need to confirm latency impact). I can push an emergency routing policy to route new sessions from eu1-az-b through backup peering if capacity allows.

elena: Before we do cross-region failover, let's confirm authentication failures are not token-service related. Jamal, can you tail the auth service logs in eu1-az-b?

jamal: Tailing auth logs now. No errors or increased 5xx on auth service itself. Most of the errors correlate with upstream gateway returning 502 before auth handshake completes. Pattern: client -> gw (retransmit) -> gw drops connection -> 502 bubbling.

sre-bot: Incident note: opened external ticket #PR-47821 with transit provider (carrier) at 09:20 UTC. Provider ACKed and is investigating ASN path.

maria: Customer updated: they see a mix of 401 + 502 when requests retry. Can we suggest a retry policy with backoff to them for now? Also want a temporary mitigation to stop flapping tokens.

jamal: Suggested customer config: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries, treat 5xx/timeout as retryable. Sent sample pseudo-code:

```
for attempt in range(3):
  try:
    res = client.call()
    if res.status == 200: break
  except TimeoutError:
    sleep((2 ** attempt) * 0.1 + random()*0.1)
```

kai: I'm prepping a routing change: add policy to prefer backup-peer for new TCP sessions originating in eu1-az-b (will leave existing sessions to avoid disruption). Rolling to gw-azb-1 first, will monitor 5xx rate. ETA 5m.

deploy-bot: :information_source: Deployment planned: route-policy/azb-backup-20260315 pushed to gw-azb-1 (dry-run -> apply). CI check passed.

elena: Proceed but watch customer complaints. Jamal, collect golden traces from Fugu and a couple of internal synthetic tests to compare pre/post.

(5 minutes pass)

kai: Applied policy to gw-azb-1. 5xx rate in az-b dropped from 19.7% -> 7.5% in ~60s. Rolling to gw-azb-2.

maria: Fugu reports immediate improvement for some users, still seeing a small subset with intermittent errors. They're happy with partial relief. :thumbsup:

jamal: Continued packet retransmits reduced after failover. Looks like we avoided the noisy path. Will keep provider ticket open to request root cause (micro-loss on specific peering).

sre-bot: SLO impact: hosted inference p95 latency EU region increased by +40ms over 09:00-09:18; error budget affected for 18 min. Recorded for postmortem.

maria: Logged customer-impact note and follow-up: offer Fugu a credits adjustment? Support suggests 2 days of service credit while we complete RCA. Please confirm billing-side.

support-bot: Billing: auto-flagging potential credit. Manual review needed - escalate to billing ops with case ID 6421.

elena: Next steps: jamal -> collect pcaps + golden traces + aws/infra flow logs and attach to provider ticket. kai -> run path validation and request BGP AS path history from carrier. maria -> confirm customer acceptance of temporary fix and coordinate credits. Ops team to draft postmortem and runbook updates for 'carrier micro-loss' playbook.

jamal: Uploads done, ticket updated. Provider responded: "we saw microbursts on interconnect interface, engineering applying shaping in core, will monitor 2hrs."

kai: Leaving routing policy in place for now to avoid re-exposure. Will schedule re-evaluation with provider after monitoring window.

elena: Thanks team. I'll tag this incident for postmortem and add runbook items: 1) check per-az 5xx split, 2) confirm auth service unaffected, 3) failover policy steps, 4) customer mitigation template.

maria: Fugu confirmed reduced errors and accepted a small service credit. Closing customer escalation after we complete RCA.

sre-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Will update status when provider confirms resolution.

jamal: Postmortem note: probable cause = transient micro-loss / buffering at provider leading to TCP retransmits and gateway 502s. Action items: add automated az-aware failover runbook, improve gateway connection-level metrics alerting for retransmit spikes, and add synthetic continuous checks per-az.

elena: Great. I'll start the postmortem doc and tag ops, infra, and support. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
